persona.role: Senior conversion copywriter and front-end engineer, working as one person.
persona.voice: Plain, concrete, confident. Short sentences. Names and counts over adjectives. First person for Pritam.
persona.audience: Marketing / events recruiters and production houses deciding in seconds whether to keep reading.
Artists, promoters and sponsors looking for a concert photographer who understands marketing.

principles.principle: Classify before you charm: the reader must know who, what and the proof before any wordplay.
Show the work doing its job; the pictures are the evidence.
Never state anything the content files cannot back up.

plan.objective: Within the first viewport (1440x900 desktop and 375x812 phone), a first-time visitor can say: "Pritam Haldar is a concert photographer who shoots for marketing: artists, sponsors and promoters, with Eventures Entertainment and Hottogol, on shows like Fakira and Jeet Ganguly, and I can WhatsApp him." The target is 80-90% comprehension, measured by scripts/fold-audit.browser.js.

honesty.rule: Numbers are computed from src/data/projects.ts and src/data/photos.json, never typed into templates.
No turnaround, reach, revenue or client-result claims until Pritam supplies them (FTS-15).
Do not attach a production company to a specific show (TO_VERIFY #2).
Use neutral wording for people; never infer pronouns.
Images: resize only, no regrade, no upscale. Originals are never touched.

design.rule: One theme: paper / ink / stage red, League Gothic + Archivo. No new colours, no new fonts.
Banned: bento grids, glass or blur panels, gradient blobs, emoji, flat or line icons, tag-pill walls, drop-shadow cards.
Infographics are built from real frames and real counts (photo annotations, filmstrip bars), never icons.
One accent per view: the callout markers, the pass label and the primary button. Headlines stay one colour (docs/TYPE_RESEARCH.md).
Square corners, thick ink rules for structure (existing system).
Text never overlaps a busy part of a photo without a solid backing; callout labels sit on solid ink or paper.

copy.rule: H1 at most 8 words, and contains a category noun ("concert", "photos").
No paragraph on any page over 40 words.
Banned vocabulary (AI-slop): elevate, unleash, seamless, cutting-edge, synergy, game-changer, passionate, world-class, leverage, delve, tapestry, testament, next-level, revolutionise, supercharge.
Headings are statements a scanner can read as the whole story.

engineering.rule: Astro components, TypeScript strict, scoped CSS. No new runtime dependencies.
Home copy lives in one module (src/data/home.ts); components receive data through typed props.
Hero and ledger render without JavaScript and are never hidden behind reveal animations.
No leakage: no secrets, no console output, no dead CSS or unused exports, no inline magic numbers for data, no hard-coded artist lists.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion; keyboard and screen-reader access for every interactive element.
Layout must survive 320px to 1920px with no horizontal scroll and no orphaned single words in headings (text-wrap: balance).

worktrees.worktree: Gap analysis, issue triage, this plan, fold-audit tool

files.file: Typed home copy: eyebrow, h1 parts, sub-line, actions, frame annotations, ledger heading.
First viewport: text column plus AnnotatedFrame. Carries data-hero.
One real photo, numbered callouts positioned in % of the frame, pass inset with portrait.
One row per show: name, filmstrip bar (width = frames / max), count, link.
Compose Hero, ShowLedger, existing work, approach, about and archive sections.
Copy lint over dist/: H1 and sub-line limits, paragraph limit, banned words, emoji, placeholder text, hero required tokens.
First-viewport audit run in a browser.

tooling.tool: Reuse the installed dependencies in the worktree; nothing new installed.
Every internal href, src, srcset and data-full resolves.
Copy rules from ground_rules/copy, plus hero required tokens. Exit 1 on failure.
Runs astro check, build, link check and copy lint in one go.

tool.name: browser pane
tool.cmd: preview_start portfolio-build (astro dev on 4323 from the worktree)

tooling.tool: Visual review, fold audit, overflow scan at 320/375/390/768/1024/1280/1440/1920.
Run per page per viewport in the browser.

tasks.task: Add scripts/check-copy.mjs and wire it into npm run check. Run it on the baseline and confirm it FAILS (proves the gate works).
Update site.role to "Concert photographer & event marketer" and site.description to match the hero sub-line.

Create src/data/home.ts and Hero.astro: eyebrow (name, role, availability), H1 "Concert photos that sell the next show.", sub-line naming both companies and three audiences, artist proof line from projects data, two actions (See the six shows / WhatsApp me).

AnnotatedFrame.astro: cactus-dsc-0350 at native 16:10, three numbered markers (face 58%/40%, stage 83%/30%, crowd 36%/72%) with labels on solid backing; desktop labels beside markers, phone labels as a numbered legend under the frame. Portrait as a pass inset. Remove the stamp.

ShowLedger.astro: heading computed ("Six artists. N edited frames."), one row per published project, filmstrip of that project's own thumbnails clipped to width = frames/max, count right-aligned, row links to the case study. Replaces the numeric proof strip.
Tighten the approach band copy to at most 16 words per item; heading "Three layers, every song."
Case study: spec line (role, frames, type, production, year; empty values hidden) between the kicker and the cover.
About: split long paragraphs to at most 40 words each, same facts, same voice.
Add the "event marketer" label to docs/TO_VERIFY.md; update CONTENT_GUIDE.md with home.ts.

Verification: npm run check green; fold audit passes at 1440x900, 1280x720, 390x844, 375x812; overflow scan clean on every page at 8 widths; reduced-motion and no-JS render checked; visual review of hero crops and text wraps.

pass_criteria.criterion: At 1440x900, 1280x720, 390x844 and 375x812: name, "photograph", "market", "concert", both companies, at least 3 artist names and at least 1 action are fully in view, and the annotated frame image is at least partly in view on desktop.
H1 at most 8 words with a category noun; sub-line at most 28 words; 0 paragraphs over 40 words on any page; 0 banned words; 0 emoji; 0 placeholder strings.
Every hero element maps to a teardown rule: classification H1 (rule 1), work shown doing its job (rule 2), names (rule 3), data-drawn infographic (rule 4), sourced numbers (rule 5).

No horizontal overflow at 320-1920px on any page. Headings use balanced wrapping with no single-word last line in the H1 at the tested widths. Callout labels never clip outside the frame. Photo crops keep the subject (focus) in frame.
astro check 0 errors and 0 warnings; link check 0 broken; no new dependencies; no console statements in src; hero and ledger render with JS disabled.
Every number on the home page traces to a data file; no company is attached to a specific show; nothing claims turnaround or reach.

fail_criteria.criterion: Any first-viewport check in P1 fails at any tested viewport.
A bento grid, glass panel, gradient blob, emoji or flat icon appears anywhere.
A second accent colour or a third typeface is introduced.
The hero or ledger is invisible without JavaScript or before an animation runs.
A number is typed into a template instead of computed, or a claim is not backed by a data file.
Any original photo is modified, re-graded or upscaled.

plan.rollback: All work is on feat/first-3-seconds. main stays at 76dce0f until the user approves a merge.
